checkpoints.description: [1/3] Shared brain ledger persistence: one LedgerLock (thread RLock + OS file lock) and shared atomic JSON write used by every brain store. [2/3] Learning, improvement, configuration, kernel, reactivity and actor ledgers reload and mutate under that lock so two processes cannot clobber each other. [3/3] Verification pass: two-instance regression tests, full suite, Phase 4 gates, ADR and codebase map.

impact_assessment.why: Brain ledgers are still process-local: each store caches state at startup and writes atomic files without a lock, so a second worker silently loses the first worker's outcomes, candidates, configuration changes, kernel blocks, reactions or actors.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every brain ledger survives concurrent writers; the last writer no longer overwrites unseen updates; one tested persistence helper replaces nine copies of the temp-file write.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: filelock is already declared; concurrency: mutating methods now hold a per-ledger OS lock, and a stuck holder makes a writer wait up to 10s then fail with Timeout; state: a .lock file appears beside each brain ledger.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Shared helper with failing-first two-instance tests for each ledger; lock scope kept to ledger mutation, not LLM or provider calls; full suite and Phase 4 gates before commit.

checkpoints.description: [1/3]-[2/3] done: LedgerLock plus atomic_write_json replace nine copies of the temp-file write; learning, improvement, configuration, kernel, reactivity and actor ledgers now reload and mutate under the lock, and evaluation/drift/state stores lock their writes. New two-instance tests cover experiences, consolidation, kernel blocks, configuration changes, actors, mutes, candidates and mutual exclusion. 86 brain tests plus 8 new tests pass.

checkpoints.description: [1/6] Remote auth fails closed: non-loopback binds refuse to start without NEUROCORE_API_TOKEN unless NEUROCORE_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_REMOTE is explicit, and middleware rejects unauthenticated non-loopback clients even when the token is unset. [2/6] CSRF compares normalized origin (scheme, host, effective port). [3/6] Sandbox fails closed on worker-start failure, exposes only explicitly permitted environment values, and its network policy rejects mixed DNS answers, validates every redirect, streams within a byte cap and honours an empty allowlist. [4/6] Retire the unused broken worker pool; add the missing scheduled-task pattern and pattern contract tests. [5/6] Memory search filters before truncation and fetches expiry in one query. [6/6] Align packaging/Docker with runtime deps, commit CI, then full verification and ADR.

impact_assessment.why: External audit of e491655 reports remote auth bypass when the token is unset, in-process sandbox fallback, unrestricted tool environment, weak network/CSRF policy, a broken unused worker pool, an invalid scheduled flow pattern and memory search underfill.
impact_assessment.benefits: Remote deployments cannot silently run unauthenticated; sandbox isolation never degrades silently; tools see only authorized secrets; redirects and oversized responses obey policy; dead execution code stops masquerading as a supported path; autonomous patterns build valid flows; semantic search returns a full page of eligible memories.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: non-loopback startup without a token now fails; ToolSandbox no longer exposes the process environment by default; allowed_domains=set() disables network; worker-pool module is removed; dependency: filelock already declared, no new runtime deps; concurrency: none added; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for each finding, updated tests for the intentional contract changes, full suite, aikit check, and an ADR recording every behavior change.
